conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Input-output section
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format: 'INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. [ file-control-paragraph ] [ i-o-control-paragraph ]' (cite.py --check 12.4.2 "INPUT-OUTPUT" -> OK §12.4.2 General format). Grammar `inputOutputSection : INPUT_OUTPUT SECTION DOT fileControlParagraph? ioControlParagraph?` is the format verbatim: both words required, period required, both paragraphs optional, FILE-CONTROL before I-O-CONTROL. environmentDivision places it after configurationSection? (the §12.2 order). Bound by DataBinder.BindFileControl (env.inputOutputSection()?.fileControlParagraph()) and BindIoControl. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/iosec): p1 both paragraphs -> runs 'OK' at 2023; p2 empty INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. -> runs 'EMPTY' at 2023 and at --std 85; p3 I-O-CONTROL before FILE-CONTROL -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'FILE-CONTROL', exit 65 (correct: the format orders them). Edition note: the 2023 spec carries no edition difference for this format, so the uniform acceptance is what the spec derives; whether COBOL-85 required FILE-CONTROL inside the section is not stated in ISO_COBOL.md and is not a basis for a verdict here. test-ref left empty: goldens exercise the both-paragraph shape (e.g. conformance:2023/l1_release_same_record_area) but none pins the optional-paragraph arms (empty section / I-O-CONTROL only) or the ordering refusal. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E row names the input-output section; the 2023 format is the only one the spec states)]

rows.subject: JUSTIFIED clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format: {JUSTIFIED|JUST} [RIGHT] (RIGHT not underlined = optional). Grammar `justifiedClause : (JUSTIFIED | JUST) RIGHT? ;` matches all arms exactly; DataBinder.cs:3985 sets Justified=true for every arm. Probe probe/justified/P1.cob (2023) and P12.cob (--std 85): `PIC X(5) JUST`, `PIC X(5) JUSTIFIED`, `PIC A(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT`, `PIC N(4) JUST RIGHT` all compile and right-justify ([   AB]). cite.py --check 13.18.32.2 "JUSTIFIED" -> OK. Existing tests exercise only the `JUSTIFIED RIGHT` spelling; no spec-derived test pins the JUST arm or the bare JUSTIFIED arm -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text:
╭ JUSTIFIED ╮ ┤ ├ RIGHT ╰ JUST ╯
> **Figure notes (JUSTIFIED clause general format syntax diagram).** `JUSTIFIED` and `JUST` are underlined in the printed standard (`JUST` is the required minimum abbreviation of `JUSTIFIED`). `RIGHT` is **not** underlined — it is an optional word. The braces require exactly one of the two spellings. No choice indicators appear in this figure.

rows.subject: JUSTIFIED clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: "JUST is an abbreviation for JUSTIFIED." (cite.py --check 13.18.32.3 -> OK §13.18.32.3 2)). JUST and JUSTIFIED are one alternative of justifiedClause and bind identically (DataBinder.cs:3985 tests only justifiedClause() presence). Probe P1: A1 `PIC X(5) JUST` and A2 `PIC X(5) JUSTIFIED` both display [   AB] after MOVE "AB"; P12 same at --std 85. No test uses the JUST spelling -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: JUST is an abbreviation for JUSTIFIED.

rows.subject: JUSTIFIED clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: "When the JUSTIFIED clause is omitted, the standard rules for aligning data within an elementary item apply (see 14.6.8 ...)" (cite.py --check 13.18.32.4 -> OK §13.18.32.4 3); --check 14.6.8 "Alignment" -> OK). StrStoreAligned(justified:false) routes to the standard left-justified StrStore; the boolean store passes justifiedRight from the item flag. Probes: P1 A5 PIC X(5) (no JUSTIFIED) <- "AB" = [AB   ]; P10 PIC N(4) <- N"XY" = [XY  ], PIC 1(4) <- B"11" = [1100] — left alignment with right space/zero fill per §14.6.8, across alphanumeric, national and boolean. The substance of §14.6.8 is owned by its own rows; this row only requires that absence of JUSTIFIED leaves the standard rules in force, which holds. No test names this rule -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: When the JUSTIFIED clause is omitted, the standard rules for aligning data within an elementary item apply (see 14.6.8, Alignment and transfer of data into data items).

rows.subject: LEAP-SECOND directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When ON is specified or implied, the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59 may be reported in the seconds position ...' (cite.py --check 7.3.17.4 OK). Determination made: never - ACCEPT FROM TIME, CURRENT-DATE, FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE and WHEN-COMPILED all read a .NET DateTime through the one Clock seam, which cannot represent second 60 (LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor summary; CONFORMANCE.md line 523). DOCUMENTATION defect only: CONFORMANCE.md line 523 and the processor summary cite this as 'A.1 item 112', but item 112 is the >= 86,400 SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT determination; the >59-seconds determination is A.1 item 111 (Annex A.1 item 111 cites '7.3.17, LEAP-SECOND directive, General rule 2'), which has no DOC-A.1-111 row in CONFORMANCE.md - acknowledged open in kb/Work PB191 'Still open, deliberately'; the DOC-A.1-111 catalog row is owned by the A.1 register. No test pins the ON-mode reported side. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility is absent in 1985; the 2002 edge is DERIVED per docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.21 - Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does not list LEAP-SECOND, so it predates 2023). The time-form / formatted-time consumers the rule bounds are COBOL-2014 intrinsics (§15.3).
rows.rule-text: When ON is specified or implied, the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59 may be reported in the seconds position of the value returned from: — the ACCEPT statement with the TIME phrase — the CURRENT-DATE intrinsic function — the FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE intrinsic function — the WHEN-COMPILED intrinsic function.

rows.subject: LEAP-SECOND directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When OFF is specified or implied, a value greater than 59 shall not be reported in the seconds position ...' (cite.py --check 7.3.17.4 OK). Holds by construction: all four sources derive from DateTime/DateTimeOffset (Second is 0..59), the COBOLNET_CLOCK pin included. unit CurrentDateOffsetDeterminationTests asserts CURRENT-DATE positions 13-14 in 0..59 citing GR1/GR3 but covers one of the four named sources only, so no test-ref is claimed. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility is absent in 1985; the 2002 edge is DERIVED per docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.21 - Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does not list LEAP-SECOND, so it predates 2023). The time-form / formatted-time consumers the rule bounds are COBOL-2014 intrinsics (§15.3).
rows.rule-text: When OFF is specified or implied, a value greater than 59 shall not be reported in the seconds position of the value returned from: — the ACCEPT statement with the TIME phrase — the CURRENT-DATE intrinsic function — the FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE intrinsic function — the WHEN-COMPILED intrinsic function.

rows.subject: LEAP-SECOND directive (whether a value greater than 59 seconds may be reported and, if so, the maximum number of seconds
rows.adjudicator-notes: §7.3.17.4 GR2 (cite.py OK §7.3.17.4 2)) leaves to the implementor whether ACCEPT TIME / CURRENT-DATE / FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED may report >59 seconds under ON; COBOL.NET answers never. Verified by code reading (AcceptSource.Time uses DateTime.Second; CobolDate.CurrentDate formats RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now(); every temporal source reads IClock -> DateTimeOffset, range 0..59) and probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s4/probe/p111.cob with >>LEAP-SECOND ON and COBOLNET_CLOCK=2016-12-31T23:59:59Z: --std 2014 and 2023 print '59 59 <compile-secs> 59'; p111b.cob at --std 2002 accepts the directive. A 23:59:60 clock pin cannot be expressed (DateTimeOffset.TryParse rejects it), so no test can pin the reported side; Pinned by —. Resolves the misnumbering PB1369 recorded (the §3 directives bullet and LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor's summary label this determination item 112; the integrator should re-key those mentions to item 111 in the same change).
rows.rule-text: LEAP-SECOND directive (whether a value greater than 59 seconds may be reported and, if so, the maximum number of seconds that may be reported). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (7.3.17, LEAP-SECOND directive, General rule 2; 14.9.1, ACCEPT statement, General rule 11; 15.21, CURRENT-DATE function, Returned value rule 1; 15.99, WHEN-COMPILED function, Returned value rule 1)

rows.subject: LINE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.35.3 "LINE and LINES are synonyms." OK (13.18.35.3 2)). The grammar takes (LINE | LINES) as one token choice and no binder or emitter path reads which was written (ScreenReportLineClauses and ReportRepetitionOf read only reportLineOperand), so the two are semantically identical by construction. Probes: LINES ARE 3 5 and LINE NUMBERS ARE 3 PLUS 2 at 2023 print on 3 and 5; LINES 3 at 2002 prints on 3. No spec-derived golden writes the LINES spelling in a report group (grep of tests/conformance) - test-needed. The over-admitted noise-word combinations (LINES IS, LINES NUMBER IS) are the FMT row's defect. || Editions (adjudicator): 2023 text. The compiler gates the LINES spelling at 2002 (grammar comment); the introducing edition is NOT derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d), so only 2002/2014/2023 were probed. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolReportWriter.g4#reportLineClause; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs#ParseArm.VisitReportLineClause

rows.subject: LISTING directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The default LISTING directive is '>>LISTING ON'.' cite.py --check 7.3.18.3 -> OK §7.3.18.3 2). The CLI (cobol --help) has no listing option and a case-insensitive search of src/Cobol.Net.* for a listing producer finds none; DirectiveStateRegistry records 'NONE HELD: ... this compiler produces none' and docs/CONFORMANCE.md (recognized-and-ignored directives paragraph) says 'no source listing is produced, so listing on/off and page ejects are inert'. GR1 ('If the compiler does not produce a source listing, the LISTING directive shall be ignored. Otherwise, the following general rules apply.') makes this rule apply only to a compiler that produces a listing, so it is satisfied vacuously; it becomes live the day a listing is added. Probe out/probe/listing-directive/lst{2002,2014,2023}.cob: >>LISTING OFF (twice), >>LISTING ON, bare >>LISTING, >>LISTING OFF interleaved with DATA/PROCEDURE lines; --std 2002/2014/2023 --run each prints A=1 / B=2 with no diagnostic, i.e. every line after OFF is still compiled and the directive has no effect. No test can observe a listing that does not exist, so test-ref is empty; the vacuous conformance rests on GR-7.3.18.3-1. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the 2023 Annex E does not list the LISTING directive as a change, so it predates 2023; the 2002 introduction of the Clause-7 directive facility is the project VCR's derivation and was not re-derived here from a 2002 annex) || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/ConditionalCompilationProcessor.cs#Process (directive consume + CompilerDirectiveCatalog.CheckOperand); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/DirectiveStateRegistry.cs#ListingDirective2002 row; src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ConstructRegistry.g.cs#listing-directive-2002
